title: Clock and Uniform
premise: In the river-port city of Vessany, Paloma Oyelaran has spent nine years as an indentured clerk for the Halvard Trading Company, hiding both their pearl-diver heritage and a wartime promise made to Ilse Marchetti, the daughter of a rival firm's owner now stranded across the border when war is declared. When a census taker's probing questions expose Paloma's unregistered status, they are forced into the open as neither citizen nor enemy—just a person with a debt of love. Navigating company politics, an inheritance claim on their late mother's diving rights, and the tightening noose of conscription, Paloma must smuggle Ilse back across the frozen river before the ice breaks. The novel ends with the crossing half-failed and half-saved: Ilse reaches the far bank, but Paloma is arrested for aiding an enemy, choosing visible love over safe invisibility—and discovering that being seen was the freedom they'd been avoiding all along.
about_author: Edmund Sandoval is the pen name of a former shipping-clerk who spent a decade cataloguing port ledgers in northern river towns before turning to fiction. Their work explores how ordinary paperwork—the census, the contract, the manifest—decides whose lives count.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. During the annual census, a meticulous taker named Odile Brac notices discrepancies in Paloma's registration and asks about parentage, birthplace, and 'other allegiances.' Paloma deflects with practiced blandness, but that night they burn a letter from Ilse rather than be caught holding it. Emotional beat: the terror of a hidden life beginning to crack open.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Pearls
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with a flashback to childhood aboard their mother's diving boat. We learn how the indenture was signed, what was surrendered, and the promise made to Ilse at the last peacetime regatta: 'If it ever turns bad, I'll get you across.' Present-day Paloma files shipping manifests for munitions now. Emotional beat: grief braided with duty; the weight of inherited silence.

chapters.title: Enemy Property
chapters.summary: Company manager Duret's POV. War is declared; all assets of the Marchetti firm in Vessany are seized, including a warehouse where Paloma once hid letters. Duret, not unkindly, warns Paloma that association with enemy names is now a chargeable offense. Emotional beat: the machinery of bureaucracy grinding personal history into contraband.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A coded message arrives via a fishmonger: Ilse is alive, trapped in occupied territory, asking if the promise holds. Paloma begins quietly preparing—forging a transit pass using skills from the ledger room, bribing a ferryman. Meanwhile Odile Brac reappears, asking sharper questions. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose; first act of open defiance.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Claim
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV interleaved with their aunt Bisi's letters. A lawyer surfaces claiming Paloma's mother held hereditary diving rights to a stretch of the river—rights that would make Paloma a legal person of standing, eligible to hold property, harder to deport. But claiming them means registering truthfully with the census. Emotional beat: identity as both trap and key.

chapters.title: Odile Brac's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The census taker has pieced together most of Paloma's story and faces her own conflict: report the anomaly and satisfy the state, or sit on it, haunted by her own brother lost to conscription. She confronts Paloma privately—not to arrest, but to ask why anyone would choose danger over safety. Emotional beat: two invisible people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Ice Thinning
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The plan crystallizes: cross at the old diving shallows where the ice is thinnest but the patrols sparsest, on the night of the company's winter gala when Duret will be distracted. Paloma signs the inheritance papers, becoming legally visible for the first time—a calculated exposure to shield the escape. Emotional beat: resolve hardening; the cost counted and accepted.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Alternating Paloma and Duret POVs. At the gala, Duret announces new security measures effective at midnight; Paloma realizes the window has shrunk by hours. A near-discovery in the coat room forces Paloma to lie directly to Duret's face. They slip out early into the cold. Emotional beat: suspense tightening; loyalty stretched to its thinnest point.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, the climax. On the river at night, Paloma meets Ilse at the shallows. The crossing goes wrong—a patrol lantern, cracking ice, Ilse falling through. Paloma dives as their mother taught them, pulls her out, and pushes her up the far bank as boots arrive behind them. Emotional beat: the promise kept at maximum price; love made undeniable and public.

chapters.title: Registered
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, months later, in a hearing room. Arrested but alive, Paloma stands trial for aiding an enemy—yet the inheritance claim and Odile's quiet testimony complicate the state's case. The sentence is commuted to supervised labor at the very docks they grew up beside. In the final scene, a letter arrives from across the river. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; invisibility abandoned, selfhood claimed.
